title: Document Request Intake Form
subtitle: A controlled intake and triage record for a targeted request for documents or data that defines authority, categories, date range, custodians, format, secure transfer, privilege and privacy handling, receipt reconciliation, deficiency follow-up, and closure, carrying facts and source evidence through qualified decision, exception escalation, secure communication, and accountable handoff.
description: This original Document Request Intake Form helps the request coordinator and supervising lawyer manage a targeted request for documents or data that defines authority, categories, date range, custodians, format, secure transfer, privilege and privacy handling, receipt reconciliation, deficiency follow-up, and closure. It opens the record, classifies the request, captures source facts and urgency, and routes a qualified accept, defer, decline, or escalation decision, while keeping jurisdiction-specific conclusions and professional judgment with authorized reviewers.
use_case: Use when the request coordinator and supervising lawyer needs one fillable record that opens the record, classifies the request, captures source facts and urgency, and routes a qualified accept, defer, decline, or escalation decision for the controlled document request. Close only after the intake disposition is supported by evidence and accepted by the named recipient.

sections.title: Legal Document Request record identity and routing
sections.guidance: Open one traceable record, establish authority, and assign accountable qualified review.

blocks.label: Legal Document Request record and responsible parties
Intake and Triage timing and route
Confidential record boundary
blocks.guidance: Use approved secure systems for protected communications and source files. Do not enter access credentials, complete account numbers, government identifiers, medical detail, or privileged source content in this routing form.

sections.title: Legal Document Request facts and source evidence
sections.guidance: Capture domain-specific facts, distinguish statements from verified evidence, and retain source references.

blocks.label: Legal Document Request matter profile
Legal Document Request evidence checkpoints
items: Request authority and recipient authority are verified before transmission
Document categories are specific, proportionate, and tied to a stated purpose
Date ranges, custodians, repositories, and excluded sources are explicit
Native, image, metadata, paper, and structured-data format needs are distinguished
Secure transfer, encryption, access, and receipt-confirmation method is assigned
Privilege, work product, privacy, protective-order, and redaction review is routed
Originals, copies, chain of custody, and return obligations are distinguishable
Received items are inventoried without placing sensitive contents in this form
blocks.guidance: Check only supported items; explain any limitation in the evidence narrative.

blocks.label: Legal Document Request evidence and action register

sections.title: Legal Document Request intake and triage control record
sections.guidance: Turn the record purpose into traceable evidence, accountable actions, and reviewable decisions.

blocks.label: Requested outcome, contact, and triage basis
Legal Document Request intake interview controls
items: The client, custodian, or authorized third party describes the requested outcome in their own terms
The controlled document request is classified before any substantive action
Material dates, amounts, persons, and assumptions are read back for confirmation
Statements are visibly separated from verified records and third-party reports
Only necessary information is requested through an approved secure route
Language, access, accommodation, and communication needs are routed
No promise of representation, result, filing, clearance, or deadline action is made
Urgent, suspicious, unsafe, or professionally restricted matters are escalated

sections.title: Legal Document Request stop conditions, exceptions, and escalation
sections.guidance: Stop when authority, identity, evidence, deadline, confidentiality, or professional-duty controls are unresolved.

blocks.label: Stop and escalate when any condition is present
items: Request authority, recipient identity, or authority to release is uncertain
Scope may be overbroad, burdensome, duplicative, or unrelated to the stated purpose
A preservation duty, litigation hold, subpoena, order, or response deadline applies
Privileged, work-product, confidential, sealed, or protected information may be included
Personal, health, financial, trade-secret, or regulated data needs special handling
Collection may alter metadata, authenticity, chain of custody, or original evidence
A source is unavailable, deleted, inaccessible, or controlled by another person
Transmission route, access rights, or recipient verification is not secure
blocks.guidance: A checked item requires immediate protective action, a named owner, qualified review, and a final disposition.

Objective facts, affected activity, containment, notifications, and review needed

blocks.label: Qualified review and record boundary
blocks.guidance: This template records operational facts and does not determine legal rights, professional duties, privilege, conflicts, consentability, deadlines, or court compliance. Follow applicable jurisdictional rules and current firm policy; route legal, ethics, privacy, tax, court, safety, and specialist questions to authorized reviewers.

sections.title: Legal Document Request qualified decision and accountable authorization
sections.guidance: Record the authorized decision separately from preliminary analysis and prevent action beyond its evidence and scope.

blocks.label: Intake and Triage qualified decision
Legal Document Request decision and execution conditions
items: Qualified lawyer approves the purpose, scope, authority, and timing
Categories, custodians, date ranges, formats, and exclusions are unambiguous
Privilege, privacy, redaction, protective-order, and security routes are assigned
Recipient instructions identify secure delivery and deficiency communication
Received material cannot be produced, filed, or disclosed without separate review
Any change in scope or recipient authority requires documented reauthorization
blocks.guidance: Check only controls supported by cited evidence; unresolved items remain open conditions.

blocks.label: Evidence considered, reasons, limits, alternatives, and required follow-up

fields.label: Evidence considered, reasons, limits, alternatives, and required follow-up

blocks.label: Preparation, qualified review, and independent authorization
blocks.guidance: Signatures acknowledge the recorded decision and scope; they do not replace required agreements, consents, notices, filings, or system approvals.

blocks.label: Decision-use limitation
blocks.guidance: Do not use this Legal Document Request record as a substitute for legal advice, a required client agreement, informed consent, court paper, discovery response, privilege review, or specialist determination. Execute only the action evidenced in the approved system of record.

sections.title: Legal Document Request completion, evidence reconciliation, and handoff
sections.guidance: Close only when the outcome is evidenced, limitations remain visible, and every open action has an accountable owner.

blocks.label: Intake and Triage outcome and primary handoff
Legal Document Request closeout evidence
items: Request transmission, recipient, date, and approved version are evidenced
Every requested category has received, unavailable, withdrawn, or pending status
Deficiencies and exceptions have an owner, due point, and escalation disposition
Received items are indexed to secure repositories and custody records
Privilege, privacy, redaction, and production review remain separate controls
Completion and any continuing preservation or return obligation are acknowledged
blocks.guidance: Unchecked items require an exception disposition or a documented reopen trigger.
